engine.name: Open 3D Engine
engine.note: Paths are relative to the O3DE checkout (o3de/). lineHash is the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the cited line with surrounding whitespace removed.

engine-version.inspect: The engine version this checkout declares; the commit identifies it exactly.

forward-pixel.inspect: The main pipeline's forward pixel shader: it evaluates the material's Surface, then EvaluateLighting, and writes diffuse and specular lighting to separate R16G16B16A16_FLOAT targets, plus the albedo, specularF0, and normal targets the full-screen passes read.

details.note: diffuse lighting goes to the diffuse target
specular lighting goes to the specular target
emission is added to the specular target

evaluate-lighting.inspect: Surface comes in by value. InitializeLightingData runs first, then the tile iterator starts, decals change the local copy of the surface, and direct lighting, forward image-based lighting, and FinalizeLightingData follow; lights come from the pixel's screen tile, since ENABLE_LIGHT_CULLING is 1.

details.note: initialised from the surface as the material made it, before any decal

direct-lighting.inspect: Every light type in turn: directional, simple point and spot (punctual), then the five area light types, each group behind a shader option that defaults to true.

details.note: simple point and simple spot lights
point, disk, capsule, quad, and polygon area lights

diffuse-specular-merge.inspect: The last opaque pass adds the diffuse and specular targets into one colour; a 2 x 2 filter smooths diffuse only where subsurface scattering marked the pixel.

details.note: the subsurface-scattering pixels only (the forward pass writes alpha -1 otherwise)

surface-data.inspect: StandardPBR's Surface (the #else branch, since DOES_CLASS_INHERITANCE_WORK_IN_ASZL is 0): lighting channels, clear coat, position, normals, base colour, metallic, roughnessLinear, roughnessA, roughnessA2, alpha, albedo, specularF0, emission, and the two occlusion factors.

details.note: the inheriting version is compiled out
diffuse ambient occlusion, 1 without an occlusion map

set-albedo-f0.inspect: The metallic workflow: albedo = GetAlbedo(baseColor, metallic), specularF0 = CalculateSpecularF0(baseColor, metallic, specularF0Factor).

surface-eval.inspect: Where the material's inputs become the Surface: base colour, metallic, and the specularF0 factor, then roughness.

material-utils.inspect: Dielectric F0 is 0.08 times the specularF0 factor, so the default factor 0.5 gives 0.04.

roughness-values.inspect: roughnessLinear is clamped to MinRoughnessLinear, squared into roughnessA, and squared again into roughnessA2; then specular AA, on by default, widens roughnessA2 by the normal's screen-space change and recomputes roughnessA and roughnessLinear from it.

lighting-data.inspect: What lighting accumulates per pixel: diffuse and specular lighting, the responses, NdotV, the BRDF texture sample, and the multiscatter compensation.

lighting-init.inspect: dirToCamera, NdotV, and the BRDF texture sampled at (NdotV, 1 - roughnessLinear).

initialize-lighting-data.inspect: diffuseResponse = 1 - FresnelSchlickWithRoughness(NdotV, specularF0, roughnessLinear), then the multiscatter compensation.

details.note: compensation, behind a shader option that StandardPBR's material property leaves off unless set

standard-init.inspect: StandardPBR runs the BasePBR initialisation and adds emission, occlusion, and, when clear coat is enabled (off by default), its share of the diffuse response.

multiscatter.inspect: 1 + specularF0 (1 / (brdf.x + brdf.y) - 1): A + B is the single-scattering energy, and the missing part is added back in proportion to F0 (Turquin 2019).

ms-option.inspect: The shader option that turns multiscatter compensation on. Its declared default is true, but StandardPBR connects it to a material property that loads as false unless the material sets it (see ms-material-property).

fresnel-schlick.inspect: Schlick's Fresnel, F0 + (F90 - F0)(1 - HdotV)^5; FresnelSchlick uses F90 = 1.

fresnel-roughness.inspect: Fresnel for light from the whole environment: the grazing value is max(1 - roughness, F0) instead of 1.

ggx-d.inspect: GGX's distribution of microfacet normals, roughnessA2 / (pi b^2) with b = NdotH^2 (roughnessA2 - 1) + 1 (Walter et al. 2007, eq. 33): a density over projected solid angle, far above 1 at the peak of a smooth lobe.

ggx-g.inspect: Height-correlated Smith masking-shadowing, returned already divided by 4 NdotL NdotV (a visibility term).

details.note: the epsilon that keeps its denominator positive

ggx-sample.inspect: A microfacet normal drawn from D for a 2D sample point (Walter 2007, eqs. 35 and 36), for the BRDF texture.

details.note: sinTheta with no guard against cosTheta rounding above 1

hammersley.inspect: The sample points: (i / N, the radical inverse of i).

diffuse-lambert.inspect: albedo NdotL / pi times the diffuse response: the diffuse term StandardPBR uses.

diffuse-disney.inspect: The normalised Disney diffuse from the Frostbite course notes, with its own Fresnel terms on entry and exit (so no diffuse response). StandardPBR does not call it; EnhancedPBR does when subsurface scattering is on, and Skin always does. DiffuseTitanfall, below it, is called nowhere in this checkout.

enhanced-diffuse.inspect: EnhancedPBR switches to NormalizedDisneyDiffuse when o_enableSubsurfaceScattering is on, and otherwise uses DiffuseLambertian as StandardPBR does.

skin-diffuse.inspect: The Skin material always uses NormalizedDisneyDiffuse.

specular-ggx.inspect: D * G * F * NdotL times the multiscatter compensation; the 1 / (4 NdotL NdotV) is inside G.

standard-brdf.inspect: StandardPBR's diffuse: DiffuseLambertian with the diffuse response, times the light; when o_clearCoat_feature_enabled (the clearCoat.enable property, false by default), less the clear coat's Fresnel. Its specular, below, is SpecularGGX, with the clear coat layered on top only then.

details.note: the clear coat, only when enabled

brdf-texture.inspect: Fills the BRDF texture once, at startup: per texel, 1024 GGX samples split the BRDF's integral into a scale A and a bias B on F0 (the split-sum approximation). Samples below the horizon add nothing, but the sums are divided by all 1024.

details.note: the sample's weight G * 4 VdotH NdotL / NdotH: BRDF times NdotL over the pdf of L, with F factored out
rows flipped, so v is smoothness

brdf-texture-size.inspect: The BRDF texture is 256 x 256 in format 24 of RHI::Format, R16G16_FLOAT: A and B as 16-bit floats.

point-light-struct.inspect: The record per simple point light: position, 1 / attenuationRadius^2, RGB intensity in candelas, the GI factor and flag, the lighting-channel mask, and padding to 16 bytes.

point-light-init.inspect: falloff = d^2 / attenuationRadius^2, and the direction to the light.

point-light-apply.inspect: Intensity / d^2 times (1 - falloff^2)^2, which reaches zero at the attenuation radius; then the diffuse and specular lighting.

details.note: the light's illuminance at the surface
d^2 held at (1 mm)^2 or more

point-light-loop.inspect: Skips the light at or beyond its attenuation radius; simple point lights get no shadows (litRatio 1).

details.note: lights of other lighting channels skipped

point-light-radius.inspect: The record stores 1 / radius^2, with the radius held at 1 mm or more.

details.note: the radius held at 1 mm or more

point-light-auto-radius.inspect: In the automatic mode, the radius where the light's irradiance falls to the cutoff: sqrt(intensity / cutoff), where intensity is the colour's perceptual luminance times the lumens.

cutoff-intensity.inspect: That cutoff: 0.1; the automatic mode is the component's default.

ibl-forward-transparent.inspect: The forward pass applies IBL to transparent materials and, through FORCE_IBL_IN_FORWARD_PASS, to Skin; it applies specular IBL when a mesh or material forward-specular option is set (both default to false). Other opaque shaders define FORCE_OPAQUE, so they get IBL from the full-screen passes.

details.note: the forward-specular options, false by default
specular IBL in the forward pass

forward-targets.inspect: What the IBL passes read back: albedo times the diffuse response and diffuse AO with specular occlusion in alpha, specularF0 with roughnessLinear in alpha, and the normal with the IBL and multiscatter flags. All of it is written from the surface the material made, before the decals EvaluateLighting applied to its own copy.

target-formats.inspect: The albedo and specularF0 targets are R8G8B8A8_UNORM, so the IBL passes see 8-bit albedo, F0, and roughness; the diffuse and specular targets are R16G16B16A16_FLOAT, and the normal target R10G10B10A2_UNORM.

diffuse-global.inspect: Diffuse IBL for opaque surfaces: the albedo target times the diffuse cubemap at the normal, times 2^m_iblExposure; the pass adds it onto the diffuse target.

reflection-global.inspect: Specular IBL for opaque surfaces: the specular cubemap along the reflection (rotated by m_iblOrientation) at mip roughness * 5, times F0 * A + B from the BRDF texture and the multiscatter compensation, times the global weight left by reflection probes, the exposure, and the specular occlusion. It writes its own reflection target, which ReflectionComposite adds onto specular.

details.note: the weight reflection probes leave to the sky

roughness-mip.inspect: The specular cubemap's mip is roughness * 5.

cubemap-coords.inspect: Turns O3DE's +Z-up world direction into the cubemap's: (-x, z, -y).

specular-preset.inspect: The default specular cubemap preset: 256 x 256 faces, GGX filter, R9G9B9E5; the High and VeryHigh presets make 512 and 1024.

diffuse-preset.inspect: The diffuse cubemap: 32 to 128 texel faces in BC6UH on PC (R9G9B9E5 on Android), a cosine filter over 180 degrees.

cubemap-ggx.inspect: The GGX filter: 256 samples per texel, and exactly six mips, which the PBR shaders expect.

filter-ggx.inspect: Per texel, with N = V = the texel's direction: GGX samples of the source, each read one mip blurrier than the mip whose texels match its solid angle, blended between two mips, weighted by NdotL and normalised. Mip m is filtered for roughness m / 5; mip 0 is not convolved.

details.note: the source mip of a sample: one level blurrier than the match

filter-cosine.inspect: The diffuse filter: taps weighted by solid angle and the positive cosine, then normalised, so the cubemap holds irradiance / pi.

vect-to-texel.inspect: The prefilter's lookups map a face's [-1, 1] onto texel indices [0, size - 1], not onto texel centres, so they sit up to half a texel off at the face's edges.

cubemapgen-license.inspect: CubeMapGen is AMD's, under a modified BSD license.

light-culling-pass.inspect: Light culling runs after the depth pre-pass and before the opaque passes: tile prepare, culling, and the remap.

tile-prepare.inspect: One thread per depth pixel, one group per tile: the tile's nearest sample and its farthest one short of the sky, then a 32-slice mask with one bit for each opaque sample's slice (and every slice between a transparent surface's nearest and farthest depth), and 1, 2, 4, or 8 bins from log2 of the depth span in metres.

details.note: the default 2x MSAA reads two samples a pixel (4x reads four, and 8x reuses the 4x path)

nvlc-constants.inspect: At most 256 entries per tile and 8 depth bins; depth is reversed (DEPTH_NEAR 1).

is-object-inside-tile.inspect: An object's depth range as a run of the 32 slices, ANDed with the tile's mask, then folded into the bins it touches.

cull-point-light.inspect: A light is kept when its sphere meets the tile's view-space box and its depth range meets the tile's mask; entries are index << 16 | bins.

details.note: appended in the order threads finish

light-culling-main.inspect: Groups in order: decals, simple point, simple spot, point, disk, capsule, and quad lights, each closed by END_OF_GROUP; polygon lights are not culled.

light-culling-remap.inspect: Per depth bin, the indices of the entries that touch it, in list order, ending with END_OF_LIST.

tile-iterator.inspect: The forward pass reads only its pixel's tile and depth bin.

polygon-not-culled.inspect: Polygon lights are compiled in (ENABLE_POLYGON_LTC_LIGHTS follows ENABLE_AREA_LIGHTS, 1), and the forward pass has a polygon loop, but the culling pass writes no polygon group: the quad group is last, so after it the remapped list holds END_OF_GROUP and END_OF_LIST, the polygon loop reads END_OF_LIST first and ends at once, and with culling on polygon lights are never shaded.

lighting-channels-test.inspect: A light shades a surface only if their lighting-channel masks share a bit; image-based lighting, the reflection passes, and decals do not test it.

lighting-channels-default.inspect: Five channels; components start with all five set (0x1F), while a mesh or light made through a feature processor alone starts in channel 0.

directional-channel-return.inspect: A directional light of another lighting channel ends the whole loop (return, not continue), so the directional lights after it are skipped too.

clear-coat-f0.inspect: The base layer's F0 under a coat: f0 = (1 - 5 sqrt(F0)) / (5 - sqrt(F0)), then lerp(F0, f0^2, factor) (Filament's base-layer change).

clear-coat-inputs.inspect: The coat's factor and roughness from the properties (times their maps), the roughness held at 0.001 or more; without a coat normal map, the vertex normal.

clear-coat-response.inspect: The diffuse response loses the coat's share: 1 - FresnelSchlickWithRoughness(NdotV, 0.04, coat roughness) * factor (IOR 1.5).

clear-coat-diffuse.inspect: Each light's diffuse is attenuated again, by the coat's Fresnel at the half vector: the coat dims diffuse twice, once through the response and once per light.

clear-coat-specular.inspect: base * (1 - Fc) + the coat's GGX, with Fc = FresnelSchlick(HdotL, 0.04) * factor and alpha = max(roughness^2, 0.0005).

details.note: ClearCoatGGX: GGX D with the coat's alpha

clear-coat-ibl.inspect: Specular IBL under a coat: the base through (1 - Fc)^2 plus the coat's own IBL (F0 0.04, times factor); direct light uses (1 - Fc) once.

clear-coat-forward-ibl.inspect: Enabling clear coat also sets o_materialUseForwardPassIBLSpecular, switching the material to forward-pass specular IBL, where ApplyIBL evaluates the coat's own lobe.

forward-ibl-stencil.inspect: A mesh whose material needs forward-pass IBL specular draws without the UseIBLSpecularPass bits, so the full-screen reflection pass skips it; UseDiffuseGIPass stays set.

ms-material-property.inspect: StandardPBR's material property for the compensation option. It has no defaultValue, so it loads as false, and material initialisation applies it to o_specularF0_enableMultiScatterCompensation: compensation is off unless the material turns it on.

bool-property-default.inspect: A Bool material property without a defaultValue loads as false.

property-init.inspect: Initialisation sets every property to its default value, which marks it dirty, so the material applies it to its shader inputs and options.

property-apply.inspect: Every dirty property is applied through its connections, a shader option among them.

ms-preset.inspect: O3DE's PBR presets set the compensation explicitly (37 of the 38 .material presets in Materials/Presets/PBR; the one without it is default_grid), this metal among them.

specular-aa-default.inspect: Specular anti-aliasing is on by default for StandardPBR materials.

specular-aa.inspect: Widens roughnessA2 by the screen-space derivatives of the normal: kernel = min(2 * 0.25 * (|dN/dx|^2 + |dN/dy|^2), 0.18), then saturate(roughnessA2 + kernel). It is compiled in (ENABLE_SPECULARAA 1).

light-culling-define.inspect: Tiled light lists are compiled in: lights reach a pixel through its screen tile.

forward-opaque.inspect: The opaque forward shader of the Standard lighting model defines FORCE_OPAQUE, so its forward-pass IBL path for transparents is compiled out.

opaque-pass-order.inspect: The opaque passes in order after Forward and ForwardSubsurface: DiffuseGlobalFullscreen (disabled when the DiffuseProbeGrid gem is on), Reflections, SkyBox, ReflectionComposite, the MSAA resolves, subsurface scattering, SSAO, then DiffuseSpecularMerge.

details.note: the reflection target added onto specular

ssao-default.inspect: SSAO runs unless a level's post-process settings turn it off: with no feature processor, no level settings, or no SSAO settings the pass is enabled, and the settings default to enabled. It modulates the diffuse target before the merge; there is no other AO method in 26.05.

ao-defaults.inspect: SSAO settings default to enabled, with blur and depth downsampling on.

reflection-target.inspect: The global specular IBL is written to its own cleared reflection target, not onto the specular target.

reflection-composite.inspect: The composite adds the reflection target onto the specular target (One, One, Add).

brdf-execute-once.inspect: The BRDF texture's pipeline runs once.

rhi-format.inspect: Counted from Unknown = 0, entry 24 is R16G16_FLOAT.

msaa-default.inspect: The main pipeline renders with 2x MSAA.

ibl-srg.inspect: The global skylight's two cubemaps, its orientation, and its exposure.

details.note: a rotation applied to the reflection direction

ibl-exposure-default.inspect: The skylight's exposure defaults to 0 stops.

point-light-luminance.inspect: A light's combined intensity is the perceptual luminance of its colour times its intensity.

clear-coat-default.inspect: Clear coat is off by default.

decal-apply.inspect: One decal on the surface: the position in the decal's box, from -1 to 1, through the transpose of its rotation and its half size; inside the box, the base map times the decal colour replaces the albedo by alpha times opacity times the angle attenuation, and the normal map bends the normal by alpha times the normal-map opacity; specularF0, roughness, and metallic are not touched, and the base map gets no colour-space conversion. Five texture arrays (0 to 4) are supported.

details.note: the rows of the transpose are the decal's axes
the angle attenuation, from the vertex normal and the decal's z axis
the base map times the colour and its factor (Multiply)
the albedo is replaced by the blended colour; a fully metallic surface (albedo 0) is still tinted only through this line
the last of the five texture arrays

decal-attenuation.inspect: The angle attenuation: the cosine between the vertex normal and the decal's projection axis, clamped to 0.55 and smoothstepped from 0.55 to 1, so a decal fades out by about 57 degrees; m_angleAttenuation blends between none (0) and all of it (1).

decal-forward.inspect: The forward pass walks the first group of its tile's list, the decals, in the order light culling sorted them, and applies each; with o_enableDecals off it still walks the group.

details.note: the option only skips the blend

decal-evaluate-order.inspect: Decals run after InitializeLightingData, on the function's own copy of the Surface (it is passed by value): the lights and forward IBL see the decalled albedo and normal, but NdotV, the BRDF sample, diffuseResponse, and the multiscatter term were computed before them, and the caller writes the albedo, specularF0, and normal targets from its undecalled surface, so the fullscreen IBL never sees a decal.

details.note: first: the lighting data is built from the undecalled surface
direct lighting reads the decalled copy

decal-options.inspect: Decals are on by default: the o_enableDecals shader option, and ENABLE_DECALS 1 (only the low-end tier 2 quality and the multi-view pipelines compile them out).

decal-cull.inspect: Decals are the first group of each tile's list: a sphere around the decal's box, of radius length(m_halfSize), meets the tile's view-space box, then its depth range meets the tile's mask, as for a point light. There is no draw-distance test in 26.05.

decal-sort.inspect: After culling, SortDecals orders the tile's decals with a bitonic sort across the group's threads: by sort key (the low byte), then by index, so a larger key is applied later and lands on top.

details.note: sorted before the group is written

decal-struct.inspect: The record the decal feature processor uploads per decal: position, opacity, rotation quaternion, half size, angle attenuation, normal-map opacity, packed sort key, texture array and index, and colour and its factor; there is no maximum draw distance in 26.05.

decal-defaults.inspect: The decal component's defaults: sort key 16, and attenuation angle, opacity, normal-map opacity, and colour factor all 1.

decal-half-size.inspect: A decal's half size is its entity's non-uniform scale times its uniform scale: a unit decal is a 2 m box.

tangent-space-normal.inspect: A normal map sample: the image builder's swapped channels swapped back, z rebuilt from x and y and kept at least 0.01.

forward-linear-sampler.inspect: The sampler ApplyDecal reads the decal textures with: trilinear, clamped in u, v, and w.

back-lighting.inspect: Transmission's back lighting per light. ThickObject (Barré-Brisebois and Bouchard 2011): saturate(V · -normalize(L + vertexNormal · distortion))^power · scale, times exp(-t · attenuation) · saturate(1 - t), with t the larger of the shadow map's thickness and the material's. ThinObject (Jimenez et al. 2010): the albedo times saturate(NdotL bias - N · L), through a diffusion kernel of the shadow thickness times 300 times the material's thickness, skipped when the distance is negative (no shadow data).

transmission-kernel.inspect: The thin mode's diffusion profile, integrated approximately: 0.25 (e^(-s t) + 3 e^(-s t / 3)), with s one over the scatter distance; it is 1 at t = 0.

transmission-finalize.inspect: The summed back lighting, times the transmission tint, joins diffuse lighting after the diffuse occlusion multiply, so occlusion does not dim it.

transmission-option.inspect: The transmission mode is a shader option, compiled in with ENABLE_TRANSMISSION 1.

transmission-defaults.inspect: EnhancedPBR's transmission properties: the mode defaults to None; thickness 0.5, tint (1, 0.8, 0.6), power 6, distortion 0.1, attenuation 4, scale 1; for thin objects, shrink factor 0.005, NdotL bias 0.1, distance attenuation 0.5, and the scatter colour (1, 0.27, 0.13) times a distance of 8.

transmission-params.inspect: The functor packs the four mode-dependent parameters into m_transmissionParams: (attenuation, power, distortion, scale) for thick objects, (shrink factor, NdotL bias, distance attenuation, scale) otherwise, and the tint with the thickness into m_transmissionTintThickness.

enhanced-brdf.inspect: EnhancedPBR's per-light BRDF is StandardPBR's unless subsurface scattering (NormalizedDisneyDiffuse) or anisotropy (AnisotropicGGX) is on; both are off by default.

sphere-light-apply.inspect: O3DE's point light (a sphere area light) lights like a simple point light, adds back lighting for transmission, and moves the specular light direction to the point of the bulb nearest the reflection ray, with an energy normalization from the bulb's size.

sphere-light-shadow-branch.inspect: The transmission distance comes from the light's shadow map inside the shadow branch; both options default to true, so the branch runs even for a light without shadows, where GetVisibility returns 1 and GetThickness 0. Thin objects then get the kernel at distance 0, its full value, rather than no back lighting.

sphere-light-shadow-option.inspect: On by default; only per-mesh shader option flags, off by default, would turn it off for meshes that no shadowed point light reaches.

per-mesh-flags.inspect: The console variable that lets lights set shader options per mesh defaults to false.

shadow-thickness-none.inspect: Without a shadow (index 0xFFFF) the thickness is 0.

sphere-light-bulb.inspect: A new sphere light's shape gets a 0.05 m radius, which SphereLightDelegate passes on as the bulb radius.

simple-point-no-backlight.inspect: A simple point light adds diffuse and specular only: no back lighting, so transmission needs another light type.

reflections-order.inspect: The reflection passes in order: the probe stencil, the blend weight, the global full-screen pass, the outer and the inner probe passes; screen-space reflections follow but are disabled by default.

probe-stencil.inspect: Each probe's inner volume is drawn with depth testing and no colour: where the surface is inside it, its back face fails the depth test and adds one to the stencil (IncrementSaturate) while its front face passes; a surface in front of the volume fails for both faces, and the front face's decrement (DecrementSaturate) cancels the back face's increment; the test (StencilRef 0 Less, 0x3F) admits only drawn surfaces.

probe-stencil-reduced.inspect: The stencil pass draws the inner volume 0.1 m smaller in each extent, to avoid seams; the stencil draw uses StencilRefs::None and the other three UseIBLSpecularPass.

probe-blend-weight.inspect: Each probe adds its weight where the surface is inside its outer box: 1 inside the inner box, otherwise the fraction of the way from the outer box to the inner one; the target is R16_FLOAT, cleared to 0, blended One/One, and only stencil 3 (outside every inner volume) is drawn.

probe-render-outer.inspect: Outside every inner volume (stencil 3), each probe adds its specular IBL times its weight over max(1, the sum of weights), times 2^exposure, into the reflection target (One/One).

probe-render-inner.inspect: Inside a probe's inner box the probe's specular replaces the reflection target, with no blend state; its stencil test is LessEqual 3, so it runs outside the inner volumes too, wherever the full inner box contains the surface.

probe-specular.inspect: A probe's specular: discarded outside the given box or where the IBL flag is off; the probe cubemap along the reflection, parallax-corrected against the outer box when enabled, at mip roughness * 5, times the compensation and F0 * A + B. Unlike the global pass it applies no specular occlusion.

parallax-obb.inspect: Parallax correction (Lagarde 2012): the reflection ray from the surface is intersected with the box from inside, and the cubemap is read toward that hit from the probe's centre.

obb-lerp.inspect: The weight between the boxes: from the inner box's closest point through the surface point to the outer box, the remaining distance over the whole, 1 on the inner box and 0 on the outer.

probe-sort.inspect: Probes draw by descending inner volume, so in the inner pass a smaller probe inside a larger one has the last word.

probe-defaults.inspect: Probe defaults: 8 m outer and inner extents, parallax correction on, the Medium bake quality (256-texel faces), and render exposure 0.

reflection-clear.inspect: The reflection target is cleared to (0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 0). The global pass runs only on stencil 3, so inside an inner volume that grey stays until the inner pass overwrites it; where the inner pass discards (the IBL flag off), the composite adds the grey.

reflection-global-stencil.inspect: The global pass's stencil test: Equal on 0x3F with StencilRef 3, so only outside every inner volume.

reflection-global-weight.inspect: The global cubemap takes what the probes leave: 1 - min(their summed weight, 1).

composite-stencil.inspect: The composite adds the reflection target where 1 <= stencil & 0x3F (LessEqual), One/One onto the specular target.

ao-placement.inspect: SSAO runs after subsurface scattering, modulating its output (the resolved diffuse target) in place, and feeds DiffuseSpecularMerge; the specular target is untouched.

details.note: the diffuse target after subsurface scattering
the merge reads the AO pass's output as its diffuse input

ssao-order.inspect: SSAO's passes: DepthDownsample, SsaoCompute, the depth-aware blur, DepthUpsample, and ModulateWithSsao on the diffuse target.

depth-linear.inspect: The linear depth SSAO reads: the view distance, from the depth MSAAResolveDepth keeps, its sample 0.

depth-resolve.inspect: The depth resolve keeps sample 0 of each pixel.

depth-downsample.inspect: Half-resolution depth takes the upper-left pixel of each 2 x 2, a real depth rather than an average.

ssao-compute.inspect: Per half-res pixel: a position and a normal from depth, then 12 local samples and 10 rotations of 4 shared ones, each weighted 1 / (distance^2 + 0.07) and counting the positive cosine to the normal; the output is (1 - AO * strength)^2.2, stored in R8_UNORM.

ssao-format.inspect: SSAO's output is 8-bit (R8_UNORM), as is the upsampled AO.

ssao-defaults.inspect: SSAO's defaults: strength 1 and a sampling radius of 0.05 of the half-res height (a screen fraction, not metres); they apply with or without level settings, but with settings present and SSAO disabled the strength is 0.

blur-defaults.inspect: The blur pass struct's own defaults are constant falloff 2/3, depth threshold 0, depth strength 50 (the fullscreen shadow's blur uses these unless the light sets its own); SSAO overrides them with 0.85, 0, and 200 whenever it has level settings.

blur-component-defaults.inspect: The SSAO blur's defaults, which SsaoParentPass pushes to both blur passes: constant falloff 0.85, depth threshold 0, depth strength 200.

blur-step.inspect: The blur runs pixel to pixel, keeping the constant falloff of the previous value, less where the depth slope changes; each output is half the chain from 8 pixels before it and half the chain from 8 after.

blur-order.inspect: The vertical blur runs first, then the horizontal one.

depth-upsample.inspect: Each full-res pixel takes its four nearest half-res pixels, weighted 3/4 near and 1/4 far on each axis and by one over the squared depth difference.

ssao-modulate.inspect: The diffuse target is multiplied by the AO in place, direct light and diffuse IBL alike.

occlusion-input.inspect: An occlusion map's red channel raised to the power of its factor; 1 without a map.

occlusion-eval.inspect: StandardPBR reads two maps: diffuse ambient occlusion and specular occlusion (cavity), each with its own factor.

occlusion-finalize.inspect: FinalizeLighting multiplies the forward pass's specular light by the specular occlusion and its diffuse light by the diffuse AO; the albedo target carries the AO and, in alpha, the specular occlusion to the full-screen passes.

occlusion-defaults.inspect: Both occlusion factors default to 1, so an assigned map is used as authored.

forward-probe-ibl.inspect: Forward-pass IBL (clear coat's) reads the mesh's own reflection probe: parallax-corrected against its outer box, and blended over the global cubemap by the inner-to-outer weight; when a probe is used its exposure replaces the skylight's.

forward-probe-pick.inspect: A mesh's forward-pass probe is the last of the probes whose outer box overlaps its world bounds, sorted by descending inner volume: the smallest.

light-index-pack.inspect: A list entry is the light's index shifted 16 bits, with its bin mask in the low bits.

cubemap-quality.inspect: The bake qualities and their face sizes: Medium, the probes' default, is 256.

probe-bake-capture.inspect: A bake renders each face as a square 90-degree view from the probe's position, near plane 0.1 m and far plane 100 m (reversed depth), into an R16G16B16A16_FLOAT target; after each face's readback the camera turns to the next face of CameraBasis.

details.note: the next face, after a readback

probe-bake-faces.inspect: The capture's faces are always 1024 texels (the image builder downsamples them); six faces, rendered one after another, each read back five frames after it is drawn.

probe-bake-write.inspect: The editor writes the six faces as one uncompressed cubemap DDS, whose name carries the quality's suffix (_iblspecularcm256 for Medium).

probe-bake-preset.inspect: The image builder picks a preset by the file's suffix: a Medium probe bake (_iblspecularcm256) uses IBLSpecular, the skylight's specular preset: 256-texel faces, GGX, six mips, R9G9B9E5.

probe-visualization.inspect: Show Visualization is on by default: each probe draws a sphere with the ReflectionProbeVisualization material at its position.

probe-visualization-surface.inspect: The visualization sphere's surface: white base colour, metallic 1, roughness 0, so it mirrors the sharpest mip.

probe-visualization-hidden.inspect: The sphere is excluded from cubemap captures, so a probe never bakes its own sphere.

punctual-group-skip.inspect: The simple point and simple spot groups of the tile's list are walked only inside `if (o_enablePunctualLights)`: with the option off, the iterator does not advance past them, so the area lights after them read the wrong groups. Decals, by contrast, keep walking their group when o_enableDecals is off.

details.note: the option that skips both groups

decal-colour-raw.inspect: A decal's colour is stored as given, with no colour-space conversion, and ApplyDecal multiplies it into the decal texture and blends the result into the ACEScg albedo.

base-colour-acescg.inspect: A material's base-colour texture is converted from linear sRGB to ACEScg, the forward pass's working space; its colour factor is converted on the CPU by TransformColor.

directional-lux.inspect: The directional light's intensity is an illuminance in lux; the component's default is 4 EV100, which is 40 lux.

directional-angular-unused.inspect: The direction adjusted for the sun's angular size is computed, but the specular call on the next line passes the plain direction to the light, so the angular diameter changes nothing.

one-shadow-light.inspect: Only one directional light casts shadows; the others are lit without shadowing.

cascade-defaults.inspect: The component's defaults: four cascades, a 1024-texel shadow map, a shadow far distance of 100 m, and an automatic split at ratio 0.9.

cascade-splits.inspect: Each cascade's far depth blends the logarithmic split near (far/near)^((i+1)/N) and the uniform split by the ratio; the last cascade ends at the far depth.

cascade-sphere-fit.inspect: Each cascade is fitted with a bounding sphere of its slice of the camera's frustum: its centre at depth (near + far) / 2 (1 + tan^2(fov/2)(1 + aspect^2)), held at the slice's far depth; the light-space box is the sphere's cube, so its size does not change as the camera turns; its position follows the camera, snapped to texels.

details.note: CalculateShadowViewAabb: the sphere's cube, extended toward the light

cascade-snap.inspect: The light-space box's corners are floored to whole shadow-map texels, so moving the camera does not make shadow edges shimmer.

cascade-select.inspect: A pixel's cascade is chosen by the shadow-map bounds, not by its depth: the first cascade whose texel coordinates hold it at least 1.5 texels inside the map.

fullscreen-shadow.inspect: Opaque forward shading reads the directional light's visibility from the full-screen shadow buffer, one value per pixel, instead of sampling the shadow maps itself.

area-lights.inspect: Quad lights are integrated with linearly transformed cosines (Heitz et al. 2016) from two 32 x 32 tables, unless the light asks for the fast approximation; disk, capsule, and polygon lights have methods of their own.

msaa-resolve-custom.inspect: The specular target's resolve scales each sample down to at most maxNeighborContrast times the brightest luminance among the four diagonal neighbours' samples, then averages the samples in the log domain (a geometric mean).

diffuse-composite.inspect: With the DiffuseProbeGrid gem enabled, as the default project template enables it, its feature processor disables DiffuseGlobalFullscreenPass in every pipeline, and its DiffuseComposite pass applies the global skylight's diffuse instead (probe grid in the level or not).

decals-advance.inspect: Decals keep walking their group of the tile's list when o_enableDecals is off, so the light groups after them stay aligned.

transform-color.inspect: Material and light colours are converted from linear sRGB to ACEScg on the CPU.

fullscreen-shadow-format.inspect: The full-screen shadow buffer is R8_UNORM at the pipeline's output size, one value per pixel, not per MSAA sample.

resolve-contrast.inspect: MSAAResolveSpecularPass sets enableNeighborClamping to 1 and maxNeighborContrast to 1.5.

diffuse-probe-grid-template.inspect: The default project template enables the DiffuseProbeGrid gem.

render-pipeline-path.inspect: The default render pipeline asset is a CVar whose default value is a per-platform trait (AZ_TRAIT_BOOTSTRAPSYSTEMCOMPONENT_PIPELINE_NAME); LowEnd is chosen by no trait, only by setting this CVar.

pipeline-trait-desktop.inspect: On Windows (and Mac and Linux, which have the same line) the pipeline is MainRenderPipeline.

pipeline-trait-mobile.inspect: On Android (and iOS, which has the same line) the pipeline is the Mobile one-target forward pipeline.

main-pipeline-passes.inspect: The main pipeline's children in order: depth pre-pass, then (in the file) light culling, shadows, the opaque parent, the transparent parent, and post-processing; within a parent, attachment dependencies decide the real GPU order.

details.note: the opaque parent (forward, fullscreen passes, merge)

depth-prepass-children.inspect: The depth pre-pass parent: an MSAA depth pass, a resolve to single-sample depth, then the linear-depth conversion SSAO and the shadow blur read.

depth-prepass-state.inspect: The pre-pass shader's depth test is GreaterEqual (the depth buffer is reversed, far = 0); it has no stencil state and no pixel stage.

forward-depth-state.inspect: The forward shader's depth test is GreaterEqual too, so a pixel passes where its depth equals the pre-pass depth (with early depth/stencil, see forward-early-z, hidden fragments are never shaded); stencil is written with Replace (write mask 0xFF, reference from the draw packet) and never read.

details.note: Replace: the last opaque draw's reference stays

forward-early-z.inspect: The forward pixel shader forces early depth/stencil testing unless OUTPUT_DEPTH is set (0 in the Base, Standard, Enhanced, and Skin shaders), so hidden fragments are rejected before they are shaded.

details.note: unless the shader writes its own depth

normal-encoding.inspect: The normal target's encoding: the normal is divided by |x| + |y| + |z|, x and y fold into two [0, 1] values, and z keeps only its sign (saturate(z * FLOAT_32_MAX)); the target stores 10 bits each.

details.note: z is one bit: its sign
the decode the fullscreen passes use

normal-flags.inspect: Two booleans in the normal target's 2-bit alpha: (flag1 + 2 flag2) / 3, decoded by comparing with 1/3, 2/3, and 1 within 0.01.

stencil-refs.inspect: The stencil bits: UseIBLSpecularPass is two bits (0x3) so the probe stencil pass can count nested volumes above it; BlockSilhouettes is 0x40; UseDiffuseGIPass is 0x80. The reflection passes read and write only the low six bits.

stencil-forward-ibl-opt.inspect: The per-draw stencil reference is built from the forward-IBL choice (0 or 0x3), always the 0x80 diffuse bit, and the 0x40 silhouette bit when the material asks for it.

lighting-model-select.inspect: A material type's lighting model picks its forward shaders (every model also gets the depth, shadow-map, and motion-vector shaders): Base only the Base forward shader; Standard and Enhanced the forward, custom-Z, and transparent variants of their own lighting; Skin only the Skin forward shader.

details.note: Skin: one shader, no transparent variant

standard-lighting-defines.inspect: The Standard model compiles out subsurface output and transmission and compiles in clear coat.

details.note: clear coat compiled in (enabled per material)

enhanced-lighting-defines.inspect: The Enhanced model compiles in subsurface output, transmission, and clear coat; its draw list is forwardWithSubsurfaceOutput.

enhanced-draw-list.inspect: Enhanced draws into the ForwardSubsurface pass (draw list forwardWithSubsurfaceOutput), which adds a sixth target, the scatter distance; Standard and Base use the forward list.

skin-lighting-defines.inspect: The Skin model compiles in dual specular, transmission, and subsurface output, compiles clear coat out, and forces IBL into the forward pass.

details.note: IBL in forward, flag cleared for the fullscreen passes
the human skin profile for thin transmission

lowend-forward.inspect: The LowEnd forward shader writes one colour: diffuse plus specular plus emission, alpha 1; there is no G-buffer for later passes to finish.

lowend-forward-target.inspect: LowEnd's forward pass has a single R16G16B16A16_FLOAT colour target, cleared to zero.

lowend-forward-ibl.inspect: The LowEnd shader applies IBL in the forward pass, since no fullscreen pass follows.

lowend-script-skin.inspect: On the LowEnd pipeline a Skin material gets no forward shader; the script logs an Error that says the combination should not be used at runtime.

mobile-pipeline-asset.inspect: The Mobile pipeline renders without MSAA (1 sample) and allows subpass merging.

mobile-pipeline.inspect: The Mobile pipeline (no depth pre-pass and no light culling pass) shades with a forward shader that turns off tiled light culling and area lights, caps decals and simple lights at 5 each, and applies IBL in the same pass.

details.note: at most 5 decals (and 5 simple point and spot lights)

deferred-inert.inspect: The deferred scaffold is switched by one CVar that defaults to false; with it off, the deferred feature processor's entry points return early, and no pass or shader template consumes a visibility buffer.

skybox-two-outputs.inspect: The sky writes its colour to both the specular target and the reflection target, so the composite pass adds it onto specular only once.

shadow-parent-order.inspect: The shadow parent runs the cascades, then the projected (spot, disk, and point) shadow maps, then the ESM builders, the fullscreen shadow, and its blur.

msaa-resolve-diffuse.inspect: The diffuse target is resolved with the plain colour resolve (a hardware average), so the packed subsurface factor in its alpha is averaged with the -1 of non-subsurface samples at edges.

tile-data-format.inspect: The tile record is one R32G32B32A32_UINT texel per 16 x 16 tile.

tile-mask-bit.inspect: A depth's slice: the position in the tile's [zNear, zFar] range, saturated, times (the float just below 32), so the bit index runs 0 to 31; samples at infinity map to the near plane.

details.note: sky samples map to the near plane

tile-mask-or.inspect: Each thread ORs its samples' slice bits into the group's shared mask, so the tile's 32-bit mask has a bit for every slice that holds opaque geometry.

tile-transparent-fill.inspect: A run of ones from one slice to another: for transparents only the nearest and farthest depth are known, so every slice between them is filled to avoid skipping a light.

tile-record.inspect: The record: x is zNear, y is zFar with the low bits replaced by log2 of the bin count, z is the slice mask, w is rewritten by the remap pass.

details.note: the span in metres over 1 m; the NVIDIA range-threshold refinement is not ported

tile-sky-replace.inspect: A sky pixel (first sample at the far plane) takes the farthest transparent depth instead; only the first sample is tested, but the result replaces both samples.

tile-unpack.inspect: Unpacking ORs the low bits of zFar back to ones, so the range is conservative (the packed bin count sits in those bits).

details.note: the overflow flag, set by the remap pass, never read by shading

tile-bin-select.inspect: The forward pass's bin: the pixel's depth as a fraction of the tile's [zNear, zFar] times the bin count (1, 2, 4, or 8).

cull-aabb.inspect: The tile's view-space box: the four tile corners at its near and far depth, unprojected, then the exact minimum and maximum of the eight points.

cull-spot.inspect: A simple spot light is tested as a hemisphere and a cone against the tile box, with a depth range from the full sphere.

cull-disk.inspect: A disk light is tested from its cone apex with a radius that adds the disk radius; the depth range uses the bulb offset instead, so the two radii disagree.

cull-capsule.inspect: A capsule light is a bounding sphere at the segment's midpoint; the capsule's own radius is not added.

cull-quad.inspect: A quad light is a sphere at its centre; a single-sided one must also have the box's bounding sphere above its plane. It is the last group the culling pass writes.

cull-end-of-list.inspect: At most 255 entries per tile survive, markers included; later entries, with their group markers, are dropped, and the overflow bit is only a flag.

tile-iterator-advance.inspect: A group ends at a value of 0xFFFE or above; each light type calls LoadAdvance once to step past the previous marker, then reads entries until IsDone.

details.note: the next entry unless the list has ended

polygon-iteration.inspect: With culling on, the polygon loop's first LoadAdvance steps past the quad group's marker and reads the list's end value, so IsDone is true and the loop never runs.

spot-falloff.inspect: Between the inner and outer cone the intensity is smoothstepped in cosine space; outside the outer cone the falloff is set to 1, so the light is skipped.

falloff-window.inspect: The window: 1 - falloff^2, squared, with falloff = d^2 / R^2, so the light fades smoothly to zero at its attenuation radius.

sphere-representative-point.inspect: The specular direction moves to the point of the bulb nearest the reflection ray: the closest-point offset from the ray, shortened by the bulb radius over its length.

details.note: the offset from the reflection ray

sphere-normalization.inspect: Energy normalisation for a widened highlight: the roughness is raised by radius / (3 distance), and the intensity is scaled by the square of (roughness over the raised roughness).

disk-light-direction.inspect: A disk's specular direction is the nearest point on the disk to the reflection ray's plane hit; the position is shifted a second time here, after an earlier shift.

capsule-intensity.inspect: A capsule's highlight takes the sphere normalisation times the ratio of the sphere's area to the capsule's, 2r / (2r + length).

capsule-auto-radius.inspect: The capsule's automatic radius returns radius times intensity: linear in intensity, where the other light types take a square root.

quad-falloff-centre.inspect: A quad light's falloff is computed from the distance to its centre only, however large the quad is.

ltc-lookup.inspect: The LTC tables are 32 x 32: the lookup is (roughness, angle of the view to the normal over a quarter turn), scaled and biased to texel centres.

details.note: the quad clipped to the horizon: 3 to 5 vertices

ltc-amplitude.inspect: The LTC integral is scaled by a second table: magnitude and Fresnel terms combine with F0 as x F0 + (1 - F0) y.

ltc-textures.inspect: The LTC tables are two DDS images, a matrix table and an amplitude table, loaded when a quad or polygon light feature processor starts.

units-ev100.inspect: EV100 to lux uses the constant 250, to nits the constant 12.5: lux = 250 * 2^EV / 100, so the directional light's default 4 EV100 is 40 lux.

units-solid-angle.inspect: A spot light's effective solid angle is pi whatever its cone, so a lumen intensity becomes candela as lumen / pi; sphere lights use 4 pi.

units-sphere-solid-angle.inspect: A sphere light's effective solid angle is 4 pi.

units-area-default.inspect: A new area light is 100 lumens.

directional-apply-lit.inspect: The directional light's shadow factor (litRatio) multiplies the finished diffuse and specular terms, after the BRDF and the intensity; back lighting is not multiplied by it.

directional-shadow-index.inspect: Only the one directional light whose index matches the view's shadow index gets the shadow's visibility; the others are lit at full strength.

depth-prepass.inspect: The pre-pass depth image is D32_FLOAT_S8X24_UINT, multisampled like the pipeline, cleared (depth and stencil) at load; the clear value is depth 0 because depth is reversed, far = 0.

details.note: the clear value (depth 0 by the struct default)

forward-albedo-target.inspect: The albedo target holds albedo times the diffuse response and diffuse AO, so a fullscreen pass only multiplies by irradiance; its alpha holds the specular occlusion.

forward-f0-target.inspect: The F0 target holds specularF0 in rgb and roughnessLinear (after specular AA) in alpha, 8 bits each.

lighting-models.inspect: A material type declares its lighting model as a string: BasePBR Base, StandardPBR Standard, EnhancedPBR Enhanced, Skin and Eye Skin.

lighting-model-standard.inspect: StandardPBR declares the Standard lighting model.

lighting-model-enhanced.inspect: EnhancedPBR declares the Enhanced lighting model.

lighting-model-skin.inspect: Skin declares the Skin lighting model (Eye does too).

roughness-input.inspect: With a roughness map the value is lerp(lower bound, upper bound, map red); without one it is the factor (default 1).

emissive-input.inspect: Emission is factor times (optionally alpha) times colour, in nits; the material's EV100 intensity is converted before it gets here.

emissive-in-specular.inspect: Emission is added to the specular target after FinalizeLightingData, so occlusion does not dim it and the later AO pass, which only touches diffuse, cannot either.

anisotropic-ggx.inspect: EnhancedPBR's anisotropic specular (when o_enableAnisotropy is on): GGX with separate roughness along the tangent and bitangent, times the multiscatter term.

dual-specular.inspect: Skin's second specular lobe: a second GGX with its own roughness and F0, mixed with the first by dualSpecFactor; both use the primary multiscatter term.

details.note: the second GGX with the dual F0 and roughness

brdf-texture-lookup.inspect: The BRDF texture's coordinates: (saturate(NdotV), 1 - roughness), read bilinearly.

shadow-caster-state.inspect: Shadow casters rasterise with a depth bias of 10 and a slope scale of 4, vertex-only with LessEqual depth.

shadow-coords.inspect: Per cascade: the world position is offset along the normal, moved into light view, pushed toward the light by shadowBias, projected to the cascade's texture coordinates; then the cascade range is picked.

details.note: toward the light, in world units

shadow-normal-offset.inspect: The normal offset is normal times the normal bias times 2 / map size: it depends on the map's pixel count, not on the cascade's world size, so every cascade uses the same offset (2.5 * 2 / 1024 = 0.0049 m by default).

shadow-is-shadowed.inspect: The None filter's test: one point sample, shadowed if the texel holds a depth (not 1) and the point's depth minus it is positive; the result is 0 or 1.

shadow-slope-bias-off.inspect: Slope bias is switched off by a constant in the shader; the slope values the CPU uploads are not used.

shadow-filter-default.inspect: The directional shadow filter defaults to None (binary, point-sampled); PCF and ESM run only if content or a CVar sets them.

shadow-use-fullscreen.inspect: Opaque forward shaders (FORCE_OPAQUE) read the fullscreen shadow buffer; only blended transparents evaluate the cascades per pixel.

fullscreen-shadow-normal.inspect: The fullscreen pass rebuilds position and normal from linear depth alone: two Gathers give the five neighbouring depths, the smaller difference per axis is crossed into a faceted normal, not the vertex normal.

shadow-blur-settings.inspect: The fullscreen shadow blur's constants are set per light: constant falloff and depth-falloff strength (component defaults 2/3 and 50); it is the same FastDepthAwareBlur as SSAO uses.

shadow-blur-radius.inspect: The blur reaches 8 pixels in each direction.

pcf-squared.inspect: Every PCF kernel returns the square of its weighted sum (this line is the first of three).

shadow-thickness-camera-span.inspect: The value that scales directional thickness is the camera's depth span, near of the first cascade to far of the last, not any cascade's light-axis range.

shadow-thickness.inspect: Thickness is the depth difference, normalised to the cascade's own light-axis range, times the camera's depth span: not metres, and a different factor in each cascade; the loop over cascades always samples the last one.

point-shadow-faces.inspect: A point light's shadow is six perspective views of 91 degrees, one per axis direction.

point-shadow-face-pick.inspect: The face is chosen by the axis with the largest magnitude in the vector from the light to the point.

ibl-diffuse-lookup.inspect: Diffuse IBL is one lookup: diffuse response times albedo times the cosine-convolved cubemap at the normal (rotated by the IBL orientation); no spherical harmonics.

diffuse-global-stencil.inspect: The diffuse IBL pass runs only where the 0x80 stencil bit is set, so every opaque mesh gets it.

reflection-composite-box.inspect: The composite box-filters the MSAA reflection samples into the specular target's every sample.

skybox-cubemap.inspect: The sky samples its own cubemap, not the IBL specular map.

ssr-default-off.inspect: Screen-space reflections are enabled only by an option that defaults to false and that the Specular Reflections component sets.

forward-ibl-ao-twice.inspect: Forward-pass diffuse IBL (transparents, Skin) multiplies in the diffuse AO here and FinalizeLighting multiplies the sum again, so it is occluded twice.

ssao-normal.inspect: SSAO's normal comes from depth alone: the smaller of the two neighbour differences per axis, crossed; mesh and normal-map normals are not used.

ssao-view-position.inspect: A view-space position from a screen UV and a linear depth, in world units: the unprojected ray times the depth.

ssao-radius.inspect: The sample radius is a fraction of the half-resolution image height (0.05 gives 27 half-res pixels at 1080p), scaled by the square root of the sample's rank; it has no world-space size, so its reach grows with distance.

ssao-local-samples.inspect: The 12 fixed taps used from the shared depth tile are pixel offsets at distance 4 and 8; the table's other entries are never used.

ssao-accumulate.inspect: Each sample adds saturate(cosine to the normal) times its weight 1 / (d^2 + 0.07), and the weight to the total; the result is the ratio, with no range check.

sss-pack.inspect: Subsurface factor and quality are two bytes packed into one integer up to 65535 and stored in the diffuse target's 16-bit float alpha, where integers above 2048 are not exact.

sss-unpack.inspect: The pass unpacks the factor and quality with frac(alpha / 65536) and frac(alpha / 256).

sss-sample-count.inspect: The convolution uses up to 200 samples, scaled by quality and cut to 30% or 60% for small on-screen footprints (80, 48, or 24 at the default quality 0.4).

sss-kernel.inspect: Burley's normalised diffusion profile as a per-channel weight: the sum of two exponentials at distance l, normalised by the smallest channel's profile at the sampled radius.

sss-barrier.inspect: The group barrier sits after the early return for pixels without subsurface scattering, so a barrier is reached by only some threads of the group.

eye-direct-lighting.inspect: Eye includes StandardPBR's BRDF, not Skin's, so its direct light is Lambertian plus one GGX; its dual-specular inputs only matter for IBL.

eye-iris-mask.inspect: A smooth iris-to-sclera mask from the distance to the pupil centre, used to blend colour, roughness, and normal.

details.note: iris refraction: a UV offset from a refracted ray, not a traced refraction

enhanced-metallic-sss.inspect: With subsurface scattering on, metallic is not read at all and stays 0.

double-sided-cull.inspect: A double-sided material turns culling off on every one of its shaders, so back faces enter the depth pre-pass, the shadow maps, and the forward pass.

back-face-normal.inspect: On a back face the surface normal is multiplied by -1, so lights and the IBL passes treat it as a surface facing the camera.

vertex-normal-unflipped.inspect: The vertex normal is never flipped for back faces; shadow offsets and both transmission modes use it.

cutout-clip.inspect: Cutout clips pixels whose alpha is below 1 - factor; the same test runs in the depth pre-pass, shadow maps, and forward pass of a Cutout material.

cutout-custom-z.inspect: Cutout sets hasPerPixelClip, which swaps the depth, shadow, and forward shaders for their CustomZ variants that have a pixel stage.

foliage-sample-material.inspect: The engine's own foliage-like test material: EnhancedPBR, double-sided, thin-object transmission with a green tint; O3DE has no foliage-specific shading.

terrain-pass-request.inspect: Terrain adds only compute (clipmap) passes before the depth pre-pass; its geometry is drawn by the stock passes.

terrain-forward-draw-list.inspect: Terrain's own forward shader joins the forward draw list, so the stock Forward pass draws it into the same five targets.

terrain-macro-constants.inspect: Without detail materials terrain is roughness 1, F0 factor 0.5 (so F0 0.04), and metalness 0.

terrain-decal-order.inspect: Terrain applies decals after its lighting data is initialised, like the main forward shader.

terrain-normal-cpu.inspect: Terrain normals are made on the CPU per vertex from height differences, normalised per axis, and stored as 8-bit integers.

terrain-normal-ps.inspect: CalculateTerrainPosition, which the vertex shader TerrainPBR_MainPassVS calls, rebuilds z from the two stored axes; exact on single-axis slopes, off where the ground slopes both ways. The pixel shader only normalises the interpolated normal.

terrain-height-blend.inspect: Height-based detail blending defaults to off in C++ and overrides the shader option's default of true, so detail materials blend by plain weights.

terrain-height-blend-option.inspect: The shader option's own default is true; the C++ configuration sets it each time.

terrain-stencil.inspect: Terrain sets both IBL stencil bits, so the fullscreen passes treat it as an ordinary opaque surface.

terrain-multiscatter-flags.inspect: Terrain's output sets the multiscatter flag from the shader option's default (true), so its fullscreen specular IBL is compensated.

terrain-no-direct-multiscatter.inspect: Terrain's lighting data keeps the multiscatter factor at 1: its direct lighting never calls the compensation.

hair-default-model.inspect: Hair defaults to the Marschner lighting model.

hair-marschner.inspect: Marschner hair: refractive index 1.55, three lobes (R, TT, TRT) built from Gaussian longitudinal terms with tilt offsets 1, 1, and 1.5 times the cuticle tilt.

hair-pass-after-opaque.inspect: Hair renders in its own passes after the opaque parent and blends into its output colour: the opaque frame's full-screen IBL, AO, and SSR have already run, so hair lights itself, with an IBL of its own (on by default).

cascade-image.inspect: The cascades share one D32_FLOAT texture array, one slice per cascade (4 x 1024 x 1024 x 4 bytes = 16 MiB by default), each slice cleared to 1.

shadow-atlas.inspect: Projected shadow maps are packed into array slices from large to small: a map half the base size takes a quarter of a slice, with an origin summed from its position digits; at the default 256 every map is a whole slice (a point light is six slices).

details.note: a map's origin in its slice

mappings.exact: uint lightingChannels; ClearCoatSurfaceData clearCoat (real factor, real roughness, real3 normal); precise float3 position; real3 normal, vertexNormal, baseColor; real metallic, roughnessLinear, roughnessA; float roughnessA2; real alpha, opacityAffectsSpecularFactor; real3 albedo, specularF0, emissiveLighting; real diffuseAmbientOcclusion, specularOcclusion. `real` is half or float by platform.
mappings.labLayout: brdf::Surface: position, normal, base_color, metallic, roughness_linear, roughness_a, roughness_a2, albedo, specular_f0, diffuse_ao, specular_occlusion, all f32, and clear_coat (factor, roughness, normal) when enabled; specular AA is applied by with_specular_aa. No vertex normal (the decals take it beside the surface), alpha, or emission; lighting channels sit on the lab's Material.

mappings.exact: real3 diffuseLighting; real3 specularLighting[MAX_SHADING_VIEWS]; real3 diffuseResponse; real shrinkFactor; float3 dirToCamera[]; real3 multiScatterCompensation; real3 emissiveLighting; real2 brdf[]; float NdotV[]; real3 translucentBackLighting (ENABLE_TRANSMISSION only); real diffuseAmbientOcclusion, specularOcclusion.
mappings.labLayout: brdf::LightingData: dir_to_camera, n_dot_v, brdf, specular_response (a local of InitializeLightingData_BasePBR), diffuse_response, multi_scatter_compensation, diffuse_lighting, specular_lighting. One view, no emission, occlusion, or transmission.

mappings.exact: SimplePointLight: float3 m_position; float m_invAttenuationRadiusSquared; float3 m_rgbIntensityCandelas; float m_affectsGIFactor; bool m_affectsGI; uint m_lightingChannelMask; float2 m_padding; padded to 16 bytes. The util keeps the direction to the light, the distance squared, and the falloff.
mappings.labLayout: brdf::PointLight: position, inv_attenuation_radius_squared, rgb_intensity_candelas, lighting_channel_mask; brdf::PointLightSample: dir_to_light, distance_squared, falloff, radius_attenuation, intensity. No GI fields.

mappings.engineName: The BRDF texture ($BrdfTexture, filled by BRDFTextureCS)
mappings.exact: 256 x 256 R16G16_FLOAT, (A, B) in RG; row y holds roughness (255 - y + 0.5) / 256; sampled bilinearly at (NdotV, 1 - roughnessLinear).
mappings.labLayout: brdf::BrdfMap: 256 x 256 f32 pairs, filled on the CPU and read bilinearly by hand in Rust and WGSL; not rounded to 16-bit floats.

mappings.engineName: ForwardPassOutput and the Forward pass's images
mappings.exact: SV_Target0 diffuse lighting and SV_Target1 specular lighting (R16G16B16A16_FLOAT); SV_Target2 albedo times diffuse response and AO, specular occlusion in A, and SV_Target3 specularF0 with roughness in A (R8G8B8A8_UNORM); SV_Target4 the normal, signed octahedron in RGB10 with two flags in A2 (R10G10B10A2_UNORM). The main pipeline renders with 2x MSAA.
mappings.labLayout: The same five targets in the same formats (RGBA16F twice, RGBA8 twice, RGB10A2), plus a false-colour target for the dock's views and an R8 target standing in for the stencil, at 4x MSAA. The CPU mirror (brdf::Ibl) rounds albedo, F0, and roughness to 8 bits (ties to even) when quantize is on.

mappings.exact: Diffuse: albedo target times the diffuse cubemap at the normal, times 2^exposure, added onto the diffuse target. Specular: the cubemap along the reflection rotated by m_iblOrientation at mip roughness * 5, times the compensation, F0 * A + B, the probes' remaining weight, 2^exposure, and specular occlusion, into its own target that ReflectionComposite adds onto specular.
mappings.labLayout: brdf::Ibl: albedo, specular_f0, roughness, irradiance, diffuse, reflect_dir, mip, prefiltered, n_dot_v, brdf, compensation, specular. On the GPU the reflection pass writes its own target and the composite adds it onto specular; no orientation or probes.

mappings.engineName: SceneSrg's specular and diffuse environment cubemaps
mappings.exact: Specular: 256 x 256 faces, six mips, R9G9B9E5 (the default preset); diffuse: 32 to 128 texel faces, BC6UH on PC; read through m_samplerEnv, a trilinear sampler.
mappings.labLayout: ibl::Cubemap: 256 x 256 x 6 mips and 32 x 32, f32 RGB, filtered on the CPU with the same filters; lookups clamp at a face's edge instead of filtering across it.

mappings.engineName: Decal (DecalStructures.azsli), the decal feature processor's record
mappings.exact: float3 m_position; float m_opacity; float4 m_quaternion; float3 m_halfSize; float m_angleAttenuation; float m_normalMapOpacity; uint m_sortKeyPacked (the key in the low byte); uint m_textureArrayIndex, m_textureIndex; float3 m_decalColor; float m_decalColorFactor; padded to 16 bytes.
mappings.labLayout: decals::Decal: the same fields, with one texture index into the lab's two procedural textures for the array and index; gShadingFrame holds five vectors per decal (decals::frame_records).
